sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.60,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Smt. Nalina H who met with road traffic accident.

2. That on 24-12-2024 at about 8-50 am., Smt. Nalina H was going to the work at Golden Seems (Garments) Factory along with her colleague Parvathamma in a bus and after alightening from the bus at Parking lot and walking towards factory from Makali- Huskur road, near Golden Seem Factory, Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of SM4SUZU Mini Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53-A-3962 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Smt. Nalina, result of which she fell down and the wheel of the said vehicle ran over the head of Nalilna H, further result of which she sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

So far as,
the petitioners have spent sum of Rs.1,00,000/- for funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
Prior to the accident, Nalina H was hale and healthy.
She was aged about 24 years.
She was working as talior at M/s Golden Seems Factory and earning sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden death of Nalina H, petitioners have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.
4. Respondent no.2/
the insurer
of Mini Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53-A-3962 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It is contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and Fitness certificate.

It is further contended that Insured vehicle was not involved in the accident, that the petitioner in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain and that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle and that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself who was crossing the road without following any traffic rules and regulations.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

2 ISSUES 1.

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioners prove that, the deceased Nalina H succumbed to the injuries sustained in a Motor Vehicle Accident that occurred on 24-12-2024 at about 8-50 a.m., at Makali - Huskur road, near Golden, Seem Factory, Dasanapurana Hobli, Bangalore North, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of SML ISUZU Mini Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53-A-3962?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
6.
The petitioner No.1 got examined himself as Pw1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P.10.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any oral evidence.

7. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No. 2 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident Nalina H (hereinafter called deceased) was going to the work at Golden Seems (Garments) Factory along with her colleague Parvathamma in a bus and after alightening from the bus at Parking lot, when walking towards factory from Makali- Huskur road, near Golden Seem Factory, Dasanapura Hobli,
Bangalore, at that time the driver of SM4SUZU Mini Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53-A-3962 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against deceased, result of which deceased fell down and the wheel of the said vehicle ran over the head of the deceased, further result of which she sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
10.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, Spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Inquest Mahazar, Post Mortem report, charge sheet, etc.,
11.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Parvathamma, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.1066/2024 of Madanayakanahally Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 106 of BNS 2023.
After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver for the offences punishable under Section 281, 106 of BNS of 2023.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent no.2 while cross examining the PW.1 has taken the defence that the accident in question has occurred within the factory premises in which the deceased was working, hence the petition filed u/Sec. 166 of MV Act is not maintainable.
The respondent no.2 has taken the aforesaid defence for the first time in the cross examination of PW.1 and they have not taken any such defence in their written statement.
Further no evidence of respondents has been adduced in support of the aforesaid defence of the respondent no.2.

It is true that the offending vehicle belong to the Golden Seem Factory in which the deceased was working and it is also true that the spot of accident is nearby the said factory but if the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the spot of accident is not within the factory premises but outside the factory premises touching to the road and at the edge of the road.

The spot mahazar and sketch clearly reveals that the petitioner after getting down from the bus while was proceeding towards factory in Huskur - Makali road, at that time the offending vehicle which came from the factory premises hit to the deceased result of which she succumbed to the injuries.
Hence, the materials placed on record clearly reveals that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No 2:
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners, it can be said that the deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
It is stated that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 24 years.
The petitioners have produced Aadhar card of the deceased which reflects the date of birth of deceased as 04-03-2000 as per Ex.P8.
Hence as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 24 years.

14. So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was doing tailoring work at M/s Golden Seems Industries Pvt Ltd., and earning sum of Rs.25,000/-.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2024, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.

Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
15.
The petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioner no.2 is the minor daughter of the deceased.
The petitioner no.2 being the minor daughter of the deceased is the dependent of the deceased.
So far as the petitioner no.1 is concerned he being the husband though is the legal representative of the deceased but not the dependent of the deceased.

16. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had minor daughter, 1/3rd of the annual income is to be deducted towards she personal expenses and remaining 1/3rd is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
17. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

It is Raghu B R vs Shashikumar G on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143097410/
4 further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

entities.text: Raghu B R vs Shashikumar G
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence in the instant case, as deceased was aged around 24 years, 40% should be added towards future prospects.

18. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/-, by adding 40% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.23,100/-, out of it if 1/3rd is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.15,400/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 15 to 25 is '18'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.33,26,400/-
(Rs 15,400/- x 18 x 12 =33,26,400/- ).
19.
Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost his wife, petitioner No.2 lost her mother, thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30 th October 2017.

20. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.

21. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/- 2 Transportation and Rs. 18,150/- funeral expenses 3 Loss of spousal Rs.96,800/-
consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium (Rs.48,400x2) 4 Loss of dependency Rs.33,26,400/-
Total Rs.34,59,500/-

Raghu B R vs Shashikumar G on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143097410/
5

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.34,59,500/- (Rupees Thirty Four Lakh Fifty Nine Thousand Five Hundred Only) and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
22. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on issue No.1 there is liability on the part of the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3 :- In the light of findings given on Issue No. 1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.34,59,500/- + cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No. II & III.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.34,60,500/- (Rupees Thirty Four Lakh Sixty Thousand Five Hundred only).
A Sum of Rs.34,59,500/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the amount with interest within 2 months from the date of award.

Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs. 6,60,500/- Petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.28,00,000/-
Out of the amount and interest

, 60% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 40% shall be released to the petitioner on proper identification.

The entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of minor petitioner no.2 till she attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioner to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minor.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
